heads.subject: fix(shell): survive deep function, source and eval nesting
heads.claim: As in Bash, the refusal is reported where it happens, on the standard error in effect there (after `f 2>/dev/null` nothing is printed, and `f 2>log` writes it into `log`), and a refused function call or eval abandons the rest of the command it is in (the next top-level command runs, with `$?` 1) rather than letting each of the 500 callers carry on as if one command had failed. If that standard error cannot be written (deep nesting under a low descriptor limit, below), the enclosing command reports the refusal instead, so it is not lost.
